title: Fit-cost benchmark: time/RAM vs feature width; locate the L4 wall; test one iterative escape
registered_in: analysis/RESEARCH_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN_v24.md section 7 Phase D (M176b) / section 12 dispatch entry (17 Aug 2026)
question: Where does the closed-form fit wall live, and is a raw iterative solver (LSQR) a drop-in escape at the sealed conditioning?

interpretation_registered_before_running.wall: the first width where the fit raises MemoryError or exceeds the registered time budget is the measured wall; widths above it require the published sketch+precondition escapes (arXiv:1305.5029, 1611.03220, 2304.12465).
interpretation_registered_before_running.escape: if LSQR reproduces the exact solve on a real-code Gram within rel 1e-9, it is a drop-in escape at this conditioning; otherwise the escape ladder defaults to the published preconditioned solvers, not raw LSQR.

synthetic.note: seeded Gaussian rows, 345 seeded labels; the Gram dominates, so n=20k is representative for the wall

escape.source: the real ms357 codes (raw, float64 Gram)
escape.note: scipy LSQR vs exact solve on G w = b with a seeded right-hand side; rel difference on the weights
